In mathematics and other scientific research, a “back to back” series of experiments is a term for an experimental method that involves testing two hypotheses at the same time with independent samples.
If you want to make one group of people use one treatment and then another group use another treatment in two separate days and then test for any possible correlations between them. For example if you administer a medication on a single day it is likely you will find that you cannot replicate the results because there is an interaction with other things.  If you perform independent control groups with just one group then you are able to control for everything. You could then compare each set of control groups against each test group.  If you do this you can really determine any interactions without any prior knowledge, since you are testing only for what happens in all those control groups.  This is similar to factorial analysis, where data are analyzed using multiple linear regressions in order to determine any underlying relationships. This method is generally described as two way ANOVA.
